title: Dracula
author: d'après Bram Stoker
desc: Un jeune avocat se rend dans un château des Carpates. Son client ne dort jamais la nuit.

p: In May 1897, Jonathan Harker, a young English lawyer, travelled to Transylvania. His job was to help a nobleman, Count Dracula, buy a house in London.
In the villages, people looked at him with fear. An old woman gave him a crucifix. "Please, take it," she said. "For your mother's sake."
At midnight, a black carriage took him up into the mountains. Wolves howled all around. Finally, he arrived at an enormous dark castle.
The Count was tall and thin, with a white moustache, very red lips and sharp white teeth. His hand was cold as ice.
"Welcome to my house," he said. "Enter freely and of your own will."
The days passed strangely. Jonathan never saw the Count during the day. They only talked at night. The Count never ate.
One morning, Jonathan was shaving with a small mirror. The Count came behind him and put a hand on his shoulder. Jonathan looked in the mirror. There was nobody behind him!
He cut himself. When the Count saw the blood, his eyes burned with a terrible fire. But he saw the crucifix, and he stepped back.
Jonathan understood that he was a prisoner. All the doors were locked. One night, from his window, he saw the Count climb down the castle wall, head first, like a lizard.
In the cellar, he found fifty boxes of earth. In one of them, the Count was lying, with his eyes open. There was fresh blood on his lips.
The fifty boxes went by ship to England. The ship arrived in a storm at Whitby. All the sailors were dead. A big black dog jumped from the ship and ran away.
In Whitby, Mina, Jonathan's fiancée, was on holiday with her best friend Lucy. Every night, Lucy walked in her sleep. Mina found her one night in the cemetery, with a dark shape bending over her.
After that, Lucy became pale and weak. There were two small red holes on her neck.
Her doctor called his old teacher from Amsterdam, Professor Van Helsing. He looked at Lucy and became very serious. He put garlic flowers around her bed and her neck.
But it was too late. Lucy died. And some days later, people saw a beautiful lady in white who walked at night and attacked children.
Van Helsing explained the terrible truth: "Count Dracula is a vampire. He has lived for four hundred years. He drinks human blood. And now he is in London."

Jonathan came back to England, ill but alive. He married Mina. With Van Helsing and their friends, they hunted the Count. They found his boxes of earth all over London and put holy bread in them, so he could not rest there.
But Dracula attacked Mina. Now she was in danger too.

The Count escaped back to his castle in Transylvania. The friends followed him. On the last evening, just before sunset, they caught his box in the snow near the castle. Jonathan cut his throat, and another friend put a knife in his heart.
In one second, Dracula's body turned to dust. And on his face, at the very end, there was a look of peace.
